bounds: two sets of inputs and three platforms; each platform may record each verdict once, so it can disagree with itself

cases.purpose: With stand-ins allowed and claimed, the kernel's answers are the ones the records call for.
Where the provider makes no claim of platform independence.
A key verified on two platforms does stand in on the third, so the rule is live.
A platform disagreeing with itself is reachable.
Planted defect: one platform's record is reused for another whatever policy says.
Planted defect: a record stands in although the key was never verified.
Planted defect: a record stands in although the provider never claimed platform independence.
Planted defect: one key agreeing on two platforms lets another key stand in: the rule the model had before, which the design text forbids.
Planted defect: a stand-in is reported as passed whatever the other platform's verdict.
Planted defect: another platform's record replaces a platform's own; nothing else changes.
Planted defect: a platform with both verdicts is reported as passed.
Planted defect: only the latest verdict for a platform is filed, so a platform disagreeing with itself is lost.
Planted defect: a status rests on another platform's record and the report does not say so.
Planted defect: one platform alone is reported as reproduced.
Planted defect: a key with both verdicts is reported as agreeing.
